properties.name: Criterion-1 baseline: 114 of 180 tools reach find_tools' top 5 on a consumer-words query, 53 do not appear in the top 10 at all — including detect_gaps, detect_defects, graph_report, loop_status, add_requirement and scan_nodes
properties.statement:
MEASURED 2026-09-11, the acceptance test for this requirement, run for the first time. ONE QUERY PER SERVED TOOL, 180 in all, each phrased as a USER states the job — never the tool's name, never a phrase from its description — sent through `find_tools` with `limit: 10` over stdio against an isolated copy of the design. Pass = the tool is in the top 5, its default reply.

    PASS (top 5)      114 of 180   (61 ranked first, 53 ranked 2–5)
    near (6–10)        13
    MISS (not top 10)  53          read-only 22 of 68 · write 31 of 112

⭐ THE MISSES ARE NOT THE OBSCURE TOOLS. They include the loop's own core: `detect_gaps` ← "what is missing or unanswered in the design that I should ask the owner about"; `detect_defects` ← "find structural problems like cycles and single points of failure"; `graph_report` ← "give me the overall health summary of the design"; `loop_status` ← "what is the design process owed right now — what should I do next". And the most basic captures: `add_requirement` ← "write down something the system must do"; `scan_nodes` ← "list all the requirements"; `get_node` ← "show me everything recorded about this one item"; `genesis` ← "start a brand new design from scratch". And the golden-thread edges: `satisfies`, `realizes`, `verifies`, `link_artifact`. `budget_report` ← "which of my declared limits is being exceeded" remains absent, as first observed.

WHAT RANKS INSTEAD is suggestive without being a diagnosis: `create_edge`, `set_interface_designation`, `set_artifact_intent` and `record_finding` appear in the top 5 for many unrelated queries — tools with long, vocabulary-rich descriptions surface for words that merely occur in them. Cause NOT established here; the open question is `dec:idea-a-problem-in-the-users-words-should-retrieve-the-tool-that-answers-it`, and the root-cause pass belongs there.

🛑 BOUNDS. (1) The corpus author had read all 180 descriptions during the sweep, so these queries are informed, not blind — a query from someone who has never seen the surface is stronger evidence and supersedes the one here. (2) One query per tool; a tool might pass on a different honest phrasing. (3) Ranks were taken with `limit: 10`; the default is 5, and a consumer sees 5. (4) Scored on the served surface as of PR #474, before any retrieval change. The full per-tool table is the acceptance record and lives beside the corpus; this node carries the totals and the misses that matter most so the number is checkable without the file.
